newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares seen tumbling further, U.S. in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares seen tumbling further, U.S. in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed considerably lower on Thursday, hit by the general market unease in Europe following the recent Wall street declines with dealers foreseeing further sizeable falls on Friday.
"I think we could see the KFX index falling by another couple of points tomorrow to around the 144-146 support point with the United States getting the blame," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 4.07 point or 2.66 per cent lower at 148.68.
The KFX June future fell 3.00 point to 148.40 with 80 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Dealers explained the major Danish index plunge as being delayed reaction after more dramatic falls in other European markets on Wednesday. Worst hit were Moeller's D/S 1912 and D/S Svendborg, which shed 6,681 and 10,264 crowns to finish at 181,319 and 263,736 respectively.

Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark, both hit by sell recommendations, ended 17 and eight crowns down at 552 and 327 respectively, while Carlsberg, downgraded by Goldman Sachs, shed eight to 382. Overall turnover for the day was 807 million crowns.
